One decision rarely stays in one layer.

The ripple across the layers

✓

Three different starting points—one connected system

You traced a strategic decision downward, a tactical plan into execution and strategic learning, and an operational problem upward into planning and redesign.

Key takeaway

Decisions move down. Feedback moves up.

The three decision layers are different, but they cannot work independently.

Strategic direction ↓ Tactical preparation ↓ Operational execution · Operational evidence ↑ Tactical adjustment ↑ Strategic learning

How the layers stay connected

Direction moves downward

Strategic choices define the structure and constraints that tactical planners and operational teams must work within.

Evidence moves upward

Operational results, bottlenecks, and repeated failures reveal where plans or long-term designs need to change.

Communication creates alignment

Tactical planning connects long-term direction with daily execution and translates feedback into coordinated action.
